description: Player 1's deck: the radiant deck, exactly the three cards BUILD's row names, so the spec can say which card each conversion lands on whatever the seed. #8 Mr. Vanilla (1, 4/4 -> 12/12, no text) is the field unit: it is cheap enough to stand on lane 1 from the first turn, its two forms differ in both numbers so a swap cannot be mistaken for a no-op, and it has no Cry, no keywords that touch the damage pipeline and no buff of its own, so 12/12 minus the damage it is carrying is the only arithmetic in the assertion (5.2: "the base-stat layer swaps immediately, damage taken and buffs are kept"). #26 Glowy Jelly Bean (3, "Choose a card in your hand; it becomes Radiant") is the hand converter, and its pick is a declared `hand` target that travels in the play action (R81): the spec points it at Knockoff Temu. #28 Knockoff Temu Glowy Jelly Bean (1) is the field converter, and it picks uniformly over the NON-RADIANT cards of the union of your library, hand and field, taking all of them when fewer exist than its count (R60), so the only way a spec can assert which card it converts is to leave exactly one candidate. A deck of these three alone does that: Player 1's opening draw is 3 (2.1, R2368000), so the whole deck is the opening hand, kept whole, the library is empty from the deal on, and Player 1 never gets The Coin (R244). Once Mr. Vanilla stands on lane 1 and Glowy Jelly Bean has gone to the graveyard making Knockoff Temu Radiant, Knockoff Temu is in the resolving zone rather than the hand when it resolves (10.1, 10.5 step 4), so Mr. Vanilla is the one non-Radiant card the union holds and the conversion lands on it. The empty library costs Player 1 fatigue from its first draw (2.4, R3): N damage on the Nth, so its hero at 30 health would first fall on its eighth turn, and the spec's sequence is over on its fourth, Knockoff Temu resolving with the hero at 20. Its seat plays under the handicap below, TUTORIAL_HUMAN's resources (R1705005) with a deckSize of 3 to match the three cards (R184).
